articles.title: The Night the Manifest Didn’t Match the Ship, and What the Terminal Learned
articles.excerpt: The night supervisor at a container terminal—call the fictional operator Harbourline—took a call from a customs broker at two in the morning. A vessel had arrived with a manifest amended twice during…
articles.body: The night supervisor at a container terminal—call the fictional operator Harbourline—took a call from a customs broker at two in the morning. A vessel had arrived with a manifest amended twice during the voyage, and the broker needed the current packing list before the inspection window opened at dawn. Harbourline’s own copy was a version behind. One clerk had the corrected file on a laptop at home, another had emailed a scanned page from a personal account, and the berth planner was working from a printout annotated in pen. No cargo was lost and no system was breached. What the terminal lost was four hours of berth time and, more quietly, some of its confidence that it knew which piece of paper was true.
articles.author: PPPing

articles.title: ArgoCD on OpenShift: managing 30 clusters with ApplicationSet and the app-of-apps pattern
articles.excerpt: Running one OpenShift cluster with Argo CD is easy. Running thirty — three environments, four regions, two tenancy models — is a different problem. At that scale, the bottleneck is never the sync engi…
articles.body: Running one OpenShift cluster with Argo CD is easy. Running thirty — three environments, four regions, two tenancy models — is a different problem. At that scale, the bottleneck is never the sync engine: it is the number of Application objects a human has to author, review and keep consistent. Thirty clusters times fifteen platform components is 450 Applications. Nobody maintains that by hand. This article describes a working topology: a single root Application (app-of-apps) bootstrapping a set of ApplicationSet resources, cluster secrets carrying environment metadata as labels, and Kustomize overlays resolving the per-environment delta. Everything is declarative, everything is in Git, and adding a cluster is a one-line label change.
articles.author: Florient DOGBE

The short version: it builds, it launches, it is open source, and it is absolutely not something you should point at your real documents yet. Below is the exact path I followed, plus the places where it goes sideways. What this project is, and what it is not The ArtCraft reimplementation ships clones of Word, Excel and PowerPoint, written in Rust, published as open source, with Claude taking part in writing the code. That last detail matters for how you treat it: the codebase moves fast, and the project is explicitly not production-ready . Think lab experiment, not daily driver.

articles.title: How to Play the Same Word Game: Rules for 2–4 Players, Scoring, and the Part the TikToks Skip
articles.excerpt: The same word game is the two-player word game that spread through Douyin and TikTok in early November: every player gets one seed word, each player secretly writes a single word they associate with i…
articles.body: The same word game is the two-player word game that spread through Douyin and TikTok in early November: every player gets one seed word, each player secretly writes a single word they associate with it, then the words are revealed. If two people wrote the same word, they score the round. Most clips online show the fun part and skip the rules. These are the exact rules we built into a free browser version at playsameword.com , plus the house variants we ended up using. What you need before you start 2 to 4 players , each with their own phone or laptop. Words are submitted secretly, so one shared screen does not work. A room code. The host creates a room and gets a 6-character code; everyone else joins with the code or a share link. 30 or 60 seconds per round.

articles.title: Legendary sci-fi magazine 'Starlog' returns as a yearly release, just in time for its 50th anniversary
articles.excerpt: Before the rise of online entertainment sites, this is where genre fans got their news
articles.body: "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection.
